state: three obsolete items whose modern replacement is not unambiguous, plus two findings that need no decision from me
method: the compiler names every still-used obsolete member; src never suppressed CS0618, so a marking the compiler does not report has no call site in the tree

measuredAt.note: 547 was invisible until the blanket CS0618 suppression in tests/Directory.Build.props was lifted

blocking.subject: every overload that configures receive endpoints inside a service instance
blocking.obsoleteReason: Job Consumers no longer require a service instance.
measuredContradiction: ServiceInstanceConfigurationExtensions.ServiceInstance carries no obsolete marking in either overload
every ConfigureEndpoints overload taking IServiceInstanceConfigurator is marked obsolete
every ConfigureServiceEndpoints overload is marked obsolete
blocking.whyIDidNotDecide: the reason names job consumers only, while a service instance also scopes endpoint names for competing instances. Dropping it from the four tests would remove that shape from the suite, and marking the entry point obsolete instead would remove a capability. Which of the two is intended is a scope decision, not a repair.

blocking.subject: the retry overloads for a pipe built directly over ConsumeContext
measuredContradiction: no UseMessageRetry overload exists for IPipeConfigurator<ConsumeContext>
the current non-obsolete UseRetry<T>(IPipeConfigurator<T>) builds RetryPipeSpecification<T>
the obsolete overloads build ConsumeContextRetryPipeSpecification, which is the consume context aware retry
blocking.whyIDidNotDecide: the named replacement does not exist for this receiver, and the overload that would bind instead has a different specification, so the migration would silently change what the retry does. Adding a UseMessageRetry for this receiver is a public API addition.

blocking.subject: InstrumentationOptions.PublishTotal and InstrumentationOptions.PublishFaultTotal
measuredContradiction: no modern replacement is named anywhere
nothing in src, tests or benchmarks reads either property, so setting them configures nothing today
the sibling properties SendTotal and SendFaultTotal are not marked
blocking.whyIDidNotDecide: directive 0073 section 1 forbids deleting an item whose modern replacement is not unambiguous. That a publish is counted as a send would be my inference, not a measurement.

reportedWithoutADecisionRequest.subject: ViciOne.ServiceBus.Tests Using_a_batch_consumer.Should_not_deliver_duplicate_messages
measured: it fails identically at 7a8c40cf, the commit the Lead replayed as 1822 of 1822
the fixture sets itself a two minute budget and sends 15000 messages whose consumer burns 50 million loop iterations per batch
with the budget raised it passes in 2 minutes 9 seconds with no duplicate and no lost message
reportedWithoutADecisionRequest.conclusion: a machine speed matter on this host, not a product defect and not caused by this block. Raising the fixture's own budget is a test change I did not make on my own.

reportedWithoutADecisionRequest.subject: EventHubIntegrationExtensions.GetCurrentProducerProvider
measured: it resolves the untyped IScopedConsumeContextProvider while the result is delivered bus bound as Bind<TBus, IEventHubProducerProvider>
the six other untyped resolutions in the tree wrap the provider per bus and were proven to isolate
the EventHub MultiBus spec is marked Category(Flaky) and needs an Azure Event Hubs namespace
reportedWithoutADecisionRequest.conclusion: a candidate, not a finding. It is not decidable locally, and cloud features need the PO's agreement first.
